## Design

### 2026-10-28: ![image_2026-10-28_122843685](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/bfR0xIxST94KbTHyBdEH2X9cGwr6dUbF/9a93395df433ccd07b2d362d1cc0269421fb6a167a80252702448ffaaabfd51f.png)

**5h**

![image_2026-10-28_122843685](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/bfR0xIxST94KbTHyBdEH2X9cGwr6dUbF/9a93395df433ccd07b2d362d1cc0269421fb6a167a80252702448ffaaabfd51f.png)

Over five hours, I developed MOODBOT, a digital prototype of a tiny desktop companion. Starting with limited coding experience, I explored how to create a futuristic interface with glowing eyes, six facial expressions and smooth blinking animations. I also developed interactive settings for adjusting the eye size and glow, alongside automatic day/night behaviour. Throughout development, I tested the features, identified improvements and refined the experience to make MOODBOT feel more lifelike. This was a valuable introduction to turning an idea into an interactive prototype.

### 2026-10-31: I deployed Bot using GitHub and Vercel. First, I uploaded my HTML, CSS and JavaScript files to a GitHub repository and connected it to Vercel to host my website. After deploying it, Vercel provided me

**5h**

I deployed Bot using GitHub and Vercel. First, I uploaded my HTML, CSS and JavaScript files to a GitHub repository and connected it to Vercel to host my website. After deploying it, Vercel provided me with a public .vercel.app address. I then went into my Vercel project settings, selected Domains and entered my chosen subdomain. I configured the required DNS records through my domain provider. Once Vercel verified my domain, it automatically enabled HTTPS, allowing me to access  Bot  through my own custom web address.
